trust_decision.summary: The AshDoubleEntry.ULID Ash type decides whether a 26-char Crockford string is a valid ULID (valid?/1 for casting) and how it maps to the 16-byte stored key (decode/1 for dumping); the first char carries only 3 bits but any of 32 symbols is accepted and silently truncated, so 4 spellings alias one row.

landing_point.why: The summary says non-canonical spellings are 'accepted'; the only ULID type in the repo is lib/ulid.ex and valid?/1 is the acceptance check reached from cast_input/2.

fix_sites.entry_point: AshDoubleEntry.ULID.dump_to_native/2 (lib/ulid.ex:48), used whenever Ash writes or filters a Transfer id / Balance transfer_id

AshDoubleEntry.ULID.cast_input/2 (lib/ulid.ex:34-40), also reached via cast_stored/2 (lib/ulid.ex:57-59) and dump_to_embedded/2 (lib/ulid.ex:159-161); public via Transfer :id attribute, Balance :transfer_id, adjust_balance/upsert_balance arguments and the balance_as_of_ulid calculation argument

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver who fixes valid?/1 could argue dump_to_native/decode is internal and only ever sees already-cast values, so the decoder's 3-bit truncation (lib/ulid.ex:203) need not be guarded.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Raw 16-byte binary input must still cast (re-encoded canonically), stored binaries must still decode, and generate_last/1 comparator ULIDs (max first char '7') used by balance_as_of must still be accepted; an over-broad fix (e.g. rejecting high first chars beyond 7, or rejecting 16-byte input) breaks balance history lookups.

O6_input_shapes: 26-char Crockford string whose first char decodes to 8-31 (e.g. '8', 'G', 'R', 'Z') via cast_input
same string passed directly to dump_to_native (bypassing cast)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: dump_to_embedded/2 given its own lightweight length-only check instead of delegating to cast_input/2
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Embedded dumping is a separate Ash.Type callback and a maintainer could plausibly inline a fast path for it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: cast_stored/2 for a 26-char string decoding and re-encoding via decode/encode (which canonicalises silently) instead of rejecting
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Stored values from legacy string columns are a plausible reason to add a tolerant load path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a calculation/filter argument path that compares the raw string ULID in-memory rather than the dumped binary
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Calculation arguments allow expressions (lib/account/transformers/add_structure.ex:74) and an in-memory comparator would be a natural optimisation.

O9_family: input canonicalisation / identifier aliasing (CWE-173, alternate encoding of a primary key)

O10_build.toolchain: mix (versions in .tool-versions); deps ash, ash_postgres, ash_money, ex_money per mix.lock
services: postgresql >= 16 for the integration suite (test/support/repo.ex:7, test/support/repo.ex:24-26)
O10_build.project_tests: test/ash_double_entry_test.exs (integration, Postgres); the ULID type itself is pure Elixir and unit-testable without a DB, as the fix's new test/ulid_test.exs does

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a first-char <= '7' check only in valid?/1 (cast_input) and leave decode/1 used by dump_to_native/2 truncating via ::3.

out_of_scope_notes: Typedoc at lib/ulid.ex:12-15 calls the value 'hex-encoded' though it is Crockford Base32; documentation only.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check); source is 17 lib files plus small tests, clearly under 5 MB, which is the basis for tiny_repo.

Whether Ash.Type default callbacks (cast_atomic, apply_constraints, array variants) bypass cast_input/valid? was not checked in the Ash dependency (deps not present in the tree); assumed to delegate to cast_input.
